confirmed: Read the entire 448-line markdown conversion and all 15 PDF pages, including the references; the document contains no appendix. The title, three authors, journal version, year 2025, volume 28(2), printed pages 295-309, and DOI 10.30191/ETS.202504_28(2).TP03 match the source (PDF p. 1, printed p. 295; document ends on PDF p. 15, printed p. 309).

One study compares two existing high-school classes, one using GenAI drawing and one conventional drawing; no random allocation of AI assistance is reported. quasi_people and observational context are supported, and core eligibility is not established (PDF p. 3, printed p. 297, Section 3.1).

The only reported random selection concerns six interviewees from each group, not allocation to assistance (PDF p. 6, printed p. 300, Section 3.3). No randomized people study with a creativity/diversity outcome was found in the full article.

Participants are 60 second-grade high-school students in New Taipei City, Taiwan, with average age 16; experimental N = 31 and control N = 29. Whole-group analyzed counts are people, not drawings or ratings; randomized counts are appropriately null, and the study is not below 50 analyzed people (PDF p. 3, printed p. 297, Section 3.1; PDF pp. 8-10, printed pp. 302-304, Tables 3-6 and 9).

Three students’ drawings were excluded for irrelevant or incomplete work, but Table 10 still divides category counts by 31 and 29. The source does not allocate these exclusions to arms (PDF p. 11, printed p. 305, Sections 4.7-4.7.1 and Table 10).

Students chose between Reed and Fisherman; drawings and descriptions were coded for characters, environmental objects, and emotions/attitudes. The category counts concern output content, whereas creative tendency is a questionnaire rather than a creativity score on the produced image (PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 298-299, Section 3.2 and Tables 1-2; PDF p. 11, printed p. 305, Table 10).

Bing AI - Copilot is described as using OpenAI DALL-E image generation; students wrote five- to ten-sentence descriptions, generated images, and combined them into videos viewed using Google Cardboard. The control class drew scenes and supplied descriptions (PDF pp. 6-7, printed pp. 300-301, Section 3.3 and Figures 4-7).
The procedure spans three weeks and Figure 3 assigns 100 minutes in Week 2 to the drawing activity (PDF p. 6, printed p. 300, Figure 3; PDF p. 13, printed p. 307, limitations).

S1-O1 reported values match Table 10: EG characters 57 (1.84), environmental objects 112 (3.61), emotions/attitudes 24 (0.77); CG 52 (1.79), 72 (2.48), and 22 (0.76). These are category counts and reported averages, not participant sample sizes, with no inferential test supplied for this comparison (PDF p. 11, printed p. 305, Table 10).

Creative tendency uses five questions on a 5-point Likert scale, adapted from Lai and Hwang (2014), with pre/post Cronbach alpha .79/.77. Pre-questionnaire means/SDs are 3.85/0.55 for EG and 3.86/0.69 for CG (PDF p. 4, printed p. 298, Section 3.2; PDF p. 9, printed p. 303, Section 4.2).

S1-O2 reported values match Table 4: EG N = 31, M = 3.72, SD = 0.59; CG N = 29, M = 3.89, SD = 0.61; t = -1.07, d = 0.28, p = .29. The conflicting prose indeed gives post means 3.73 and 3.88 with SDs 0.59 and 0.61, t = -1.07, p = .64; the form correctly preserves this inconsistency (PDF p. 9, printed p. 303, Section 4.2 and Table 4).

The achievement posttest totals 100 points: 20 multiple-choice questions worth 60 points, eight multiple-answer questions worth 32 points, and one open-ended question worth 8 points (PDF p. 4, printed p. 298, Section 3.2).

S1-O3 reported values match Table 3: EG N = 31, M = 71.77, SD = 9.60; CG N = 29, M = 66.07, SD = 8.31; t = 2.45*, d = 0.64, *p < .05. Section 4.1 indeed instead gives EG SD = 9.06 and exact p = .02; the form correctly flags the SD inconsistency (PDF p. 8, printed p. 302, Section 4.1 and Table 3).

All numerical result values in the one-line finding match the relevant tables or adjacent prose; only the learning-achievement p-value locator needs the correction listed above (PDF pp. 8-9 and 11, printed pp. 302-303 and 305, Sections 4.1-4.2 and Tables 3, 4, 10).

This is a primary empirical study, not a synthesis, so the empty synthesis defaults are appropriate. No supplementary material, preregistration, or data/code availability link is stated in the article; acknowledgment names funding from the National Science and Technology Council of Taiwan rather than company sponsorship (full PDF; funding on PDF p. 13, printed p. 307).
summary: The full journal article reports one intact-class comparison with 60 students and no reported random assignment to AI assistance, supporting quasi_people/observational classification. The reported results match the PDF, but six corrections address the drawing unit count, subgroup-count wording, exact-delay claim, unsupported rater coding, and two source locators.
